newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean wine exports up sharply in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Chilean wine exports up sharply in first quarter.

text.p: Chilean wine and liquor exports soared 65 percent in the first quarter of the year to $79.6 million over the same period last year, the Agriculture Ministry reported.
Wines classified as "denominacion de origen", which includes higher-class varieties, grew 31 percent to $48.7 million while other wines grew 6.5 percent to $16.8 million.

Wine in recipients of up to two liters rose 8.4 percent to $10.6 million, champagne exports doubled to $1.6 million, while pisco exports fell by about half to $123,000 in the first quarter, the ministry said.

The United States continued to be the largest market for Chilean wine, accounting for $11.1 million, followed by Britain at $8.2 million and Denmark at $3.2 million, all in the first quarter of the year, the ministry said.
Top wine exporters include Vina Concha y Toro, Cervecerias Unidas wine unit San Pedro, and Santa Rita.
